fields.what: First version of the standard library: the structures bodies share (counts, sequences, texts, value types), the published standards (web, ECMAScript, text, algorithms, measures, system), the design patterns, and the loading of a page with its browser realization

Obligations: the families of what a shipment must prove, derived from what it reaches (Verified, Served, Applied, Reviewed, Checked and the vocabulary CheckWays, Ruled, Safe), each with acceptance criteria

Scenarios of its own: an environment Test where it plays what it offers, its realizations kept in memory chosen there, and three scenarios (the seeded draws, the device in memory, the tooling in memory); a check whose program verifies reached code is an obligation of Verified and closes its gap; a page chooses an option of a list (BrowserPage.choose, Playwright's selectOption, recorded in memory); the CSS id selector, the hunk and range separator of unified differences, fs.watch's change event
Verified obliges only what a machine runs: the scenarios and the checks a program runs; a check made by hand is the family Checked's business, and leaves the gap of what it alone verifies

The language named by its names (#trame/kernel, #trame/kinds/*), the rules written as bodies (g79), the quantities Time and Ratio (g80), what the platform may do and typed commands (module effects, g83–g84), where a package comes from (PackageSources, g87)
Where a package comes from publishes too, and names its origins (PackageOrigins: by its path, from a registry); node:module's registerHooks in the table of the platform
Time counts milliseconds too, and the bodies that met JavaScript's clocks receive Time instead of the prelude's ms and elapsed
A package's source says which versions it holds; npm's words to install what a project names
The library ships its versions through its own graph: NextVersion, under VersionMode; the command maker verified by a scenario

The device's services as ports: preferences, the device's languages, a voice, the screen kept awake, with the browser's realizations and, for scenarios, realizations kept in memory; the Screen Wake Lock API
HTML and CSS: the HTML, WAI-ARIA, SVG and CSS standards move here from Trame, with the elements a page is made of (headings, header, main, footer, nav)

The frames of the screen as a port (AnimationFrames, with the browser's and, for scenarios, frames turned by hand), what a voice said and whether the screen is kept awake for scenarios, the SVG namespace and the pointer-down event
Seeded draws: a number, an integer between bounds, an element by its weight, the same from the same seed
The voice says whether the device can speak, and picks a voice of the language asked (Chrome on Android); language tags
The voice keeps what it last failed with; Web Speech and Web Audio standards

Rules a project applies with their parameters (Reaches, NeverReaches, Linked, WithoutEffects, WordsOf); the SDLC's tooling: program commands, project files, a headless browser, each for a machine and in memory; class selectors in CSS
